text:
It was a record-breaking occasion in more ways than one. David Moyes made history for Everton, edging clear of Harry Catterick by overseeing his 593rd game in charge of the club, but calamitous defending ruined the Scot’s evening and defeat to Brentford was inevitable after James Tarkowski received his first red card in 351 Premier League appearances.
Those in Tarkowski’s corner will claim the Everton captain’s tackle on Yehor Yarmoliuk might not even have been given as a foul back in the day. This, though, was not a “game’s gone” moment. “He’s not that sort of player,” is not something anyone will ever say about Tarkowski. The defender’s back catalogue features plenty of orange card tackles and there was always likely to come a time when his luck ran out.
Everton, whose muted performance denied them the chance to go fifth, should not bother complaining about Matthew Donohue’s intervention from Stockley Park after Tarkowski went in on Yarmoliuk with his studs raised late in the first half. After all Tarkowski’s first red since he was playing for Brentford in the Championship had no great bearing on the result. Brentford were already 2-0 up when their former player went off, Keane Lewis-Potter’s quickfire double putting them in control, and were in control from start to finish.
The only disappointment for Keith Andrews was his side failing to score more than four. Vitaly Janelt added a third in style and Fábio Carvalho made it 4-0 to underline Brentford’s superiority. They are up to sixth and demonstrated that they have the tools to challenge for European qualification.
With Igor Thiago unavailable after his controversial red card against Brighton it fell to Callum Wilson to lead the line for Brentford. It was the striker’s first league start since joining from West Ham last summer and he was involved in the game’s first noteworthy attack, pinching possession in midfield before the move ended with Jaidon Anthony shooting wide.
Everton sat in a low block but were troubled by Brentford’s speedy wing play and sharp interchanges in midfield. Mikkel Damsgaard floated through the middle to test Jordan Pickford and the hosts should have scored in the 19th minute. Wilson was involved, dropping off to release Michael Kayode, but the right-back dragged his shot wide.
Everton’s carelessness in possession invited trouble and their luck soon ran out. They were caught out by a long ball down the left and were undone when a poor clearing header led to a moment of brilliance from Anthony, the winger’s cushioned touch with the outside of his right foot running for Lewis-Potter to beat Pickford thanks to a deflection off Jarrad Branthwaite.
Brentford love to make the most of Lewis-Potter’s attacking instincts after converting him into a left-back. A winger in his Hull days, his runs on to cutbacks are always a threat but Everton were not paying close enough attention. They were abysmal in the first half and faced more pressure when Vitaliy Mykolenko conceded a free-kick after losing Dango Ouattara. Damsgaard crossed, Everton were all at sea and Lewis-Potter scored via another deflection, this time off Thierno Barry.
Everton were dour. They sought a lifeline through Harrison Armstrong, Caiomhín Kelleher tipping the midfielder’s shot over, but composure eluded them. Tarkowski, seemingly rattled by the barracking from the home crowd, could have few complaints after storming into a challenge on Yarmoliuk. The initial call was a yellow but Tarkowski’s boot was high, the follow-through looked cynical and the force was excessive, convincing Craig Pawson to show a red after a VAR review.
Everton adjusted after going down to 10, Merlin Röhl going to right-back, and Barry drew a superb save from Kelleher just before half-time. Brentford had to switch on. They were intense at the start of the second half and Ouattara nodded wide from Damsgaard’s cross.
Moyes had introduced Jack Grealish for the ineffective Tyrique George. Grealish, back in the squad for the first time in over a month, tried to run at Kayode. Everton were too honest to lie down and almost pulled a goal back after an hour, only for Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall’s cross to run away from Barry.
Brentford recognised the threat and killed Everton off when Janelt used his left foot to belt a formidable shot past Pickford from 25 yards. This is an open season and both of these sides will feel they can push for Europe. On this evidence Brentford look likelier to challenge the established order.
They completed the humiliation when Carvalho came off the bench to bundle in a corner in added time.
